security_audit.summary: The audit found no evidence of malicious prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden execution. The static alerts are caused by Markdown code examples, CI snippets, tool names, secret placeholder references, and a CWE link. The CI examples still require normal approval, least-privilege credentials, and human validation before use.

remediation.issue: Example commands and secret references may be copied without review.
remediation.suggestion: State that external scanners and CI automation should run only with user approval and least-privilege credentials.

remediation.issue: The instructions reference resources/implementation-playbook.md, but the package only includes SKILL.md.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the missing resource reference or include the playbook so users do not follow a broken path.

content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security, performance, and maintainability issues when changes move quickly. This skill provides structured AI review workflows, scanner guidance, and comment formats for pull requests.
actual_capabilities: Defines triage steps for pull request size, change type, and risk area.
Maps review tasks to tools such as CodeQL, Semgrep, SonarQube, Snyk, and TruffleHog.
Provides prompt patterns for security, performance, architecture, and testing review.
Shows structured review comment fields with severity, category, references, and fix examples.
Includes CI workflow examples for static analysis, AI review, comment posting, and quality gates.
Outlines review summaries across critical, high, medium, and low findings.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples; it does not execute scanners by itself.
External tools, API keys, and CI permissions must be configured separately.
AI-generated findings still need human verification before blocking a release.
The package includes only SKILL.md, despite referencing an optional playbook resource.

use_cases.title: Audit Sensitive Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Review authentication, authorization, input handling, and dependency changes before merge.

use_cases.title: Standardize Review Criteria
use_cases.description: Create repeatable severity rules, comment formats, and quality gates for engineering teams.

use_cases.title: Design CI Review Pipelines
use_cases.description: Plan workflows that combine scanners, AI review, pull request comments, and release gates.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Pull Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a focused change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review the attached diff for bugs, tests, and maintainability. Return concise findings with file, line, severity, reason, and suggested fix.

prompt_templates.title: Check Security Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this authentication or data access change for OWASP risks, secret exposure, missing authorization, and unsafe input handling. Prioritize exploitable issues.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI Review Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for automated pull request checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CI plan that runs CodeQL, Semgrep, SonarQube, dependency checks, and AI review for this repo. Include triggers, permissions, outputs, and quality gates.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Enterprise Review Policy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced policy design for large teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given our repository standards, risk tolerance, and past false positives, design a review routing policy for automatic comments, human escalation, and release-blocking findings.

output_examples.input: Review a 120-line login pull request with changed session handling.
output_examples.output: The skill returns prioritized findings, including missing session invalidation, weak test coverage, and exact review comments for the affected lines.

output_examples.input: Plan CI review automation for a TypeScript API.
output: A scanner matrix covering CodeQL, Semgrep, SonarQube, and dependency checks.
A pull request comment workflow with severity labels and quality gate rules.
A list of required secrets and permissions to configure outside the skill.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a large refactor touching service boundaries.
output_examples.output: The skill separates automated checks from human review areas, then flags compatibility, ownership, testing, and architecture risks.

best_practices: Run deterministic static analyzers before AI review so prompts include concrete evidence.
Require human review for security-sensitive, large, or architecture-changing pull requests.
Store API keys in CI secret managers and restrict repository token permissions.
anti_patterns: Asking the model to approve a pull request without line-level evidence.
Letting AI-generated comments block releases without human confirmation.
Running scanners with broad credentials or on untrusted forks without permission checks.

faq.question: Does this skill run CodeQL or Semgrep automatically?
faq.answer: No. It describes workflows and prompts. Users must install and run tools in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it replace human reviewers?
faq.answer: No. It helps with triage, repeatable checks, and suggested comments. Humans should decide architecture and release risk.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility. The examples also discuss other model providers.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: Only if you implement the CI examples. Keep keys in secret managers and use least privilege.

faq.question: What review areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers security, performance, architecture, maintainability, testing, and AI or ML-specific concerns.

faq.question: Is the referenced playbook included?
faq.answer: No. The current package contains SKILL.md only, so use the main instructions as the available source.
